headline: South Korea's Forests Rise From War's Ashes
meta_description: After severe degradation from the Korean War, South Korea planted over 10 billion trees, transforming forests to cover 63% of the country.
summary_short: South Korea planted more than 10 billion trees to restore forests devastated by war. Today, forests cover 63% of the country with 29 times more standing wood than decade…
body:
South Korea's mountains were severely degraded after the Korean War, leaving vast stretches barren and depleted. The country responded with an ambitious reforestation campaign, planting more than 10 billion trees over the following decades.

The effort has paid off dramatically. Forests now cover 63% of South Korea's land, a remarkable recovery from wartime devastation. Today, the country's forests contain 29 times more standing wood than they did in their most depleted state—a testament to what sustained commitment to restoration can achieve.

This transformation represents far more than environmental recovery. It shows how a nation can heal its landscape and rebuild what conflict destroyed, one tree at a time.
quick_facts: South Korea planted more than 10 billion trees
Forests now cover 63% of the country
Standing wood volume increased 29 times over
Severe degradation followed the Korean War
